US.source: US Census Bureau, Current Population Survey Annual Social and Economic Supplement (CPS ASEC), Table HINC-01
US.method: Household-count-weighted mean household size, computed by allocating each of the 41 published $5,000-wide income brackets (plus open-ended $200k+ bracket) proportionally across income deciles by cumulative household share, then weighting each bracket's published mean household size by its overlap with each decile band. NOTE: HINC-01 is used instead of HINC-04 because HINC-01 publishes mean household size directly cross-tabulated with income brackets at fine granularity; HINC-04 cross-tabulates by presence-of-children x household type, not by income decile, so does not support decile-level household-size estimation as directly.

DE.source: Eurostat ilc_lvph01 (Average household size, national avg 2024) shape-modeled across income deciles
DE.method: Modeled (Tier C): OECD Family Database SF1.1 publishes household size by household TYPE, not by income decile, and Eurostat SILC does not publish a cross-country household-size-by-income-decile table. We use the UK's own published decile-level shape (ONS Family Spending / Living Costs and Food Survey: D1=1.3 people, D10=3.3 people, ratio 2.538x) combined with the empirically observed convex decile-shape from US Census HINC-01 (income-bracket-weighted mean household size) as the normalized cross-country curve shape, rescaled per country so its decile average matches that country's own published national average household size (Eurostat ilc_lvph01 2024 for DE/NO/SE/FI/CH; ONS 2024 for UK; Japan national statistics for JP). See build_household_size_intl.py for full methodology and rationale.
